title: A Benchmark for Evaluating Faithfulness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
abstract: We introduce a benchmark that measures whether answers from retrieval-augmented generation systems are faithful to the retrieved documents. We compare automatic faithfulness metrics against human judgments and find that LLM-as-judge metrics correlate best.

title: Detecting Hallucinations in RAG Pipelines with Token-Level Uncertainty
abstract: Hallucination detection for RAG systems remains difficult. We propose a token-level uncertainty signal that flags unsupported claims in generated answers and improves detection F1 over prior baselines on three QA datasets.

title: Measuring Retrieval Quality for Long-Context Question Answering
abstract: We study how retrieval quality affects downstream answer accuracy in long-context question answering, and propose recall-oriented evaluation metrics for retrievers used in generation pipelines.

title: Grounded Answer Generation: Do Citations Help Users Trust Model Outputs?
abstract: We run a user study on citation-backed answers from language models that ground their outputs in retrieved evidence, analysing when users verify sources and when grounding errors go unnoticed.

title: Protein Structure Prediction with Equivariant Graph Networks
abstract: We present an equivariant graph neural network for protein structure prediction that improves accuracy on held-out families while reducing training compute.

title: Sample-Efficient Reinforcement Learning for Quadruped Locomotion
abstract: We train quadruped robots to walk on rough terrain with a model-based reinforcement learning method that needs ten times fewer environment steps than model-free baselines.

title: Efficient Attention Kernels for Large Vision Transformers
abstract: We design memory-efficient attention kernels for vision transformers that speed up training on high-resolution images without accuracy loss.

title: Federated Learning Under Label Noise
abstract: We analyse federated learning when client labels are noisy and propose a robust aggregation rule with convergence guarantees.

title: Curriculum Prompting for Mathematical Reasoning
abstract: We show that ordering few-shot examples from easy to hard improves chain-of-thought accuracy of language models on math word problems.

title: Speech Recognition for Low-Resource Languages with Self-Supervised Pretraining
abstract: We pretrain speech encoders on unlabelled audio from low-resource languages and fine-tune them for recognition, cutting word error rate substantially.
